title: Combining Human Organoids and Organ-on-a-Chip Technology to Model Intestinal Region-Specific Functionality
protocol: Prepare the human organoid growth medium following the manufacturer's instructions and supplement it with 100 µg/mL primocin.
Prepare human microvascular endothelial cell growth medium following the manufacturer's instructions, supplementing with 1:20 vol/vol FBS and 50 μg/ml primocin instead of 100 μg/ml.
Resuspend Y-27632 in sterile 0.1% BSA in DPBS to prepare a 10 mM stock solution.
Aliquot Y-27632 into sterile microtubes and store at -20 °C for up to 6 months.
Resuspend CHIR99021 in sterile DMSO to prepare a 5 mM stock solution.
Aliquot CHIR99021 into sterile microtubes and store at -20 °C for up to 6 months.
Mix organoids dissociation solution with DPBS solution in a 1:1 ratio and supplement it with 10 µM Y-27632 stock solution.
Initiate HIMEC culture 7 days before seeding onto the chip.
Use HIMECs only at passage 1-6 for chip seeding.
Add 5 mL of attachment factor solution to a T150 flask; incubate at 37°C for 1 min and discard.
Add 19 mL of endothelial cell growth medium pre-warmed at room temperature to the flask.
Thaw a frozen vial of HIMEC (2 million cells/vial) in a 37°C water bath.
Transfer the contents of the vial into the T150 flask and gently rock to distribute cells evenly.
Place the flask in a 37°C incubator overnight for cell adhesion.
Replace the medium with 20 mL of endothelial cell growth medium pre-warmed at room temperature on day 2.
Repeat replacing the medium every 3 days thereafter.
Cultures should reach 90% confluency on the day of harvest for chip experiments.
Obtain chips from a commercial supplier.
Unpack the chips and position them in the chip cradle placed in a square Petri dish.
Label the front side of each chip carrier with experimental conditions.
Reconstitute ER-1 in 10 mL of ER-2 reagent to make a final concentration of 0.5 mg/mL.
Gently push 50 μL of the ER-1 solution through both channels of the chip.
Remove any excess ER-1 solution from the surface of the chip using an aspirator.
Inspect the chips to ensure all have received the ER-1 solution and remove air bubbles if present.
Incubate the chips inside the UV lamp chamber for 15 min on the Consistent setting.
Aspirate the ER-1 solution from both channels after incubation.
Wash any residue of the ER-1 solution with 200 μL of ER-2.
Push 200 µL of sterile Dulbecco's phosphate-buffered saline (DPBS) through the channels.
Leave DPBS in the channels until the next step.
Reconstitute collagen IV using sterile cell culture grade water to a final concentration of 1 mg/mL.
Prepare aliquots and store them at -20°C until use.
Reconstitute fibronectin using sterile cell culture grade water to a final concentration of 1 mg/mL.
Prepare aliquots and store them at -20°C until use.
Mix collagen IV with solubilized basement membrane matrix (BMM) in sterile cold DPBS for the top channel at concentrations of 200 µg/mL and 100 µg/mL, respectively.
Mix collagen IV with fibronectin in sterile cold DPBS for the bottom channel at concentrations of 200 µg/mL and 30 µg/mL, respectively.
Aspirate DPBS from both channels of the chips.
Replace with the appropriate ECM working solution for each channel.
Inspect each chip to ensure it has received the coating solution.
Push through more coating solution until all air bubbles are fully removed.
Add sterile DPBS to the chip cradle.
Place the Petri dish containing the chips in a 37 °C incubator.
Incubate overnight to allow the ECM proteins to form ionic bonds with the activated PDMS membrane.
Transfer the ECM-coated chips to the BSC.
Gently aspirate the ECM coating from both the channels of the chips.
Wash both channels with 200 µL of organoid growth medium and endothelial cell growth medium, respectively.
Store the washed chips in a 37°C incubator until proceeding with endothelial cells seeding.
Bring the HIMEC culture flask to the BSC.
Wash using sterile DPBS.
Add 3 mL of dissociation solution to the flask.
Place it in the 37°C incubator for 2 min to allow for complete cell detachment.
Collect the cells in a 15 mL conical tube.
Add endothelial cell growth media until it reaches 10 mL.
Sample 15-20 µL of the cell suspension for cell counting.
Centrifuge at 150 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant from HIMECs.
Re-suspend the HIMECs to a density of 8-10 x 10^6 cells/mL in endothelial cell growth media.
Seed endothelial cells into the bottom channel of the chip.
Remove all the media from the bottom channel using a 1,000 µL pipette.
Introduce 10-15 μl of HIMEC suspension into the bottom channel of the chip.
Inspect the chip right after seeding to ensure optimal seeding density (80%-90% coverage).
Wash the channel with 200 μl endothelial cell growth media if needed and repeat the seeding procedure.
Invert the Petri dish immediately after seeding each batch of six chips.
Place the Petri dishes into the 37°C incubator for 30 min to 1 h until HIMECs attach to the membrane.
Push 200 μl endothelial cell growth media through the bottom channel inlet to remove unattached cells and replenish nutrients in the media.
Wash away unattached cells in the top channel with 200 μl organoid growth medium supplemented with 5 µM CHIR99021 and 10 µM Y-27632.
Seed organoid fragments in the top channel of the chip.
Follow procedures described in Fujii et al. for isolation of human intestinal crypts and establishment of organoid cultures.
Use duodenal and colonic organoids to generate duodenum and colon chips, respectively.
Perform a pilot evaluation of cell density in the organoid suspension culture to achieve an optimal seeding density of 8 million cells/mL.
Aspirate the supernatant from three wells of the organoid culture plate.
Add 500 μL of ice-cold BMM dissociation solution to each well.
Detach solubilized BMM from the plastic using a plastic scraper.
Collect the organoid suspension into a sterile low protein binding conical tube using an ice-cold pipette.
Incubate on ice for 60 min, mixing every 15 min by gently shaking the tube.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and add 2 mL of Trypsin.
Incubate at 37°C for 30 min to digest the organoids to the single-cell level.
Add 10 mL of complete organoid growth medium to stop the enzymatic reaction.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of complete organoid growth medium.
Count the total number of cells using a hematocytometer according to standard methods.
Store the suspension on ice for 60 minutes.
Mix every 15 minutes by gently shaking the tube.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Proceed with mixing supernatant and cell pellet if a transparent gel layer is observed.
Add an equal volume of BMM dissociation solution to the mixture.
Store on ice for an additional 10 minutes.
Centrifuge again at 300 x g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Repeat steps until no solubilized BMM residues are present.
Discard the supernatant after removal of all BMM residues.
Resuspend the organoid pellet with organoid digestion solution to ensure complete submersion.
Incubate at 37°C for 1-3 minutes.
Add Advanced DMEM/F-12 to stop enzymatic reaction, using four times the volume of the digestion solution used.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend organoid fragments pellet in complete growth medium supplemented with 5 µM CHIR99021 and 10 µM Y-27632 to achieve a concentration of 8 million cells/mL.
Prepare 360 μL aliquots of the cell suspension in sterile 1.5 mL low protein binding tubes.
Aspirate the medium from the top channel of each coated chip.
Add 30 μL of cell suspension into the top channel of each chip.
Incubate chips overnight at 37°C to allow organoid fragments to adhere to the ECM-coated membrane.
Allow media temperature to equilibrate to room temperature.
Subject media to vacuum-driven filtration for 10 min using a vacuum pump and PVDF filter conical tubes.
Open portable modules in the BSC.
Place portable modules on culture module trays.
Add 3 mL of pre-equilibrated complete organoid growth medium supplemented with 5 µM CHIR99021 and 10 µM Y-27632 to the top inlet reservoir.
Add 3 mL of pre-equilibrated endothelial cell growth medium in the bottom inlet reservoir.
Add 300 μL of the same media in the respective outlet reservoirs.
Bring the trays to the 37°C incubator and slide them into the culture module.
Use controls on the screen of the culture module to run the "Prime Cycle" (1 min long).
Repeat the Prime Cycle to ensure sufficient droplets have formed for successfully connecting the chips.
Wash both channels of the seeded chips with 200 μL of the respective media to remove any bubbles or cell debris.
Leave small droplets of media on the ports after the wash.
Slide the chip carrier into the portable module.
Place the portable modules on the trays, and then into the culture module.
Use the controls on the screen of the culture module to program the appropriate organ chip culture conditions (flow rate and stretch).
Set the flow rate to 30 µL/h for standard duodenum chip culture conditions.
Set the flow rate to 60 µL/h for standard colon chip culture conditions.
Prepare fresh media every 48 hours by adding 2 ml of fresh medium to the inlet reservoirs.
Pause the culture modules and bring the trays to BSC.
Aspirate media in all the reservoirs.
Replenish with fresh media.
Bring the trays back and restart the flow.
Allow cells to grow to 100% confluence before applying cyclic strain.
Pause the culture module when introducing stretch to ongoing fluidic cultures.
Change stretch settings on screen to 2%, 0.2 or 0.15 Hz, depending on organ type.
Restart the culture module with new stretch settings.
After 24 hours, pause the culture module again.
Adjust stretch settings to 10%, 0.2 or 0.15 Hz, as applicable.
Restart the culture module with adjusted stretch settings.
Prepare stock solutions of 20 mM Rifampicin and 100 mM Vitamin D3 using sterile DMSO.
Dilute the stock solutions in complete organoid growth medium to achieve 20 µM Rifampicin and 100 nmol/L Vitamin D3.
Dilute DMSO in complete organoid growth medium to achieve a final concentration of 0.1% DMSO for vehicle control.
Replace media in all inlet reservoirs with dosing media containing inducers or vehicle control.
Restart the flow at 30 µL/h after replacing the media.
After 24 h, replace the media with inducing solution.
Prepare fresh daily inducing solutions and replenish every 24 h for 48-72 h experiment duration.
Prepare probe substrate solution of Testosterone in Advanced DMEM/F12 at 200 µM concentration on the day of harvest.
Aspirate dosing medium from all reservoirs in BSC.
Wash top and bottom inlet reservoirs with warm Advanced DMEM/F12 and endothelial cell growth medium, respectively.
Replace wash medium with 1 mL probe substrate solution.
Perfuse chips at a high flow rate of 1,000 µL/h for 5 min.
Aspirate both top and bottom outlet reservoirs after perfusion.
Incubate chips under constant flow of 300 µL/h for 1 h.
Aliquot 200 µl of stop solution containing acetonitrile with 0.1% formic acid in pre-labeled tubes on ice.
Stop the flow after 1 hour of treatment.
Bring trays back to BSC.
Collect 100 μL of effluent from the top outlet reservoir.
Add collected effluent to corresponding tube containing stop solution.
Place tubes immediately on dry ice.
Store samples at -80°C.
Extract and analyze samples using HPLC or LC-MS/MS techniques.
Monitor formation of metabolite-6β-hydroxytestosterone (6β-OH-T).
Determine total protein content per chip by performing a Bradford assay.
Calculate CYP enzyme activity in pmol/min/mg protein.
Express CYP activity as the ratio of induced activity to vehicle control activity.
Lysis cells for mRNA analysis if required.
Detach chips from portable modules.
Place detached chips in a Petri dish.
Wash channels with 200 μL of sterile DPBS.
Block the bottom channel outlet with a 200 µL filter pipette tip.
Perfuse 50 µL of the dissociation solution through the bottom channel.
Incubate for 2 min at room temperature.
Inspect to confirm complete detachment of the endothelial cells.
Pipette up and down 1-2 times.
Remove the dissociation solution from the channel.
Repeat wash.
Block the top channel outlet with a 200 µL filter pipette tip.
Perfuse 75 µL of protein lysis buffer through the top channel.
Leave the pipette tip inserted to block the top channel inlet.
Incubate for 5 min at room temperature.
Pipette up and down 5-10 times.
Collect the cell lysates in a pre-labeled 1.5 mL tube.
Repeat steps until complete detachment of cells is observed.
Collect the cell lysates in the same 1.5 mL tube.
Store them at -80 °C until analysis.
Extract the protein fraction according to standard methods.
Quantify total protein using the Bradford assay.
Prepare intestine chip for lysis following steps 8.3.2.1 to 8.3.2.2.
Block the outlet of the top channel using a 200 µL filter pipette tip.
Perfuse 150 µL of RNA lysis buffer through the top channel.
Leave the pipette tip inserted to block the inlet of the top channel.
Incubate for 2 min at room temperature.
For lysis using a phenol-based RNA lysis buffer, use 350 µL of the reagent.
Pipette up and down 5-10 times and collect the cell lysates in a pre-labelled 1.5 mL tube.
Repeat the step with another 150 µL of RNA lysis buffer and collect.
Store the cell lysates at -80 °C until analysis.
Extract total RNA from the cell lysates using an RNA purification kit.
Reverse-transcribe into cDNA using a reverse transcriptase kit.
Carry out real-time PCR using a real-time PCR cycler and the appropriate primers and buffer.
Quantify the results using the 2-ΔΔCt method.
Prepare a 100 μg/mL stock solution of IFNγ in sterile cell culture water.
Store the stock solution at -80°C.
Use a fresh stock of IFNγ for each experiment, avoiding more than three freeze-thaw cycles.
Dilute the stock solution in degassed endothelial cell growth medium to achieve a final concentration of 10-100 ng/mL.
Remove the medium from bottom channel inlet reservoirs and replace it with 3 mL of the IFNγ containing medium.
Refresh the IFNγ dosing medium daily.
Perfuse the chips at a high flow rate of 1,000 μL/h for 5 min to initiate IFNγ treatment.
Switch the flow rate back to 60 μL/h and continue the fluidic culture.
Pause the culture module and bring the trays to the BSC.
Label and prepare a 96-well black-walled plate with 100 μL of DPBS per well.
Collect and add 50 μL of effluent from all the reservoirs to the respective wells using a 200 μL multi-channel pipette.
Dilute medium containing 100 µg/mL of 3 kDa dextran Cascade Blue 1:3 in DPBS.
Perform serial dilutions using a three-fold dilution of endothelial cell growth medium in DPBS.
Read the fluorescence at 375 nm excitation and 420 nm emission using a plate reader.
Wash cells on-chip with 200 μL of DPBS for each channel, three times.
Perfuse 200 μL of fixative solution (4% PFA in DPBS) in each channel.
Incubate for 15 min at room temperature.
Repeat the washing step 9.2.2.1.
Store washed chips for up to 7 days at 4°C if needed.
Permeabilize cells using 200 µL of permeabilization solution (0.1% Triton-X 100 in 10% normal donkey serum (NDS) in DPBS).
Incubate the cells with permeabilization solution for 30 min at room temperature.
Repeat the washing step 9.2.2.1.
Block the cells using 200 µL of blocking solution (10% NDS in DPBS).
Incubate the cells with blocking solution for 1 h at room temperature.
Dilute anti-Zonula Occludens 1 (ZO-1) antibody, anti-Occludin antibody, and anti-Claudin 4 antibody in antibody solution (5% NDS in DPBS) at a concentration of 1:100 each.
Perfuse 200 µL of the primary antibody solution through each channel.
Incubate with primary antibodies overnight at 4°C.
Repeat the washing step 9.2.2.1.
Dilute secondary antibodies in antibody solution (1:300, 5% NDS in DPBS).
Perfuse 200 µL of this solution through each channel and incubate for 2 h at room temperature.
Repeat the washing step 9.2.2.1.
Optionally add phalloidin to the secondary antibody solution if desired.
Prepare a 50 µg/mL solution of DAPI in DPBS.
Perfuse each channel with 200 μL of the DAPI solution.
Incubate at room temperature for 15 min.
Repeat the washing step.
Store stained chips at 4°C for up to 14 days.
Isolate and quantify the total amount of protein from epithelial cells as described in step 8.3.2.
Dilute samples with DPBS to a final concentration of 400 µg/mL.
Quantify levels of total and cleaved caspase 3 using the caspase 3 detection kit following the manufacturer's protocol.
Use effluents collected from the outlet of both channels of the colon chip to quantify secreted acute-phase proinflammatory cytokines, following protocols provided by the manufacturer.
Perform a 5-fold dilution for V-PLEX Vascular Injury Panel 2 Human Kit.
Perform a two-fold dilution for V-PLEX Human Proinflammatory Panel II.
